universalAnswers.whatHappened: UN climate chief Simon Stiell publicly asked AI companies for measurable climate action and resource-use information on September 21.
universalAnswers.plainLanguageIdentity: A public policy speech pressing company leaders to disclose and reduce resource use, rather than a new regulation.
universalAnswers.evidenceBasis: Original UNFCCC transcript plus AP reporting on the surrounding Climate Week debate.
universalAnswers.evidenceLimits: No new binding rule, company compliance result, local project study or causal household-bill analysis is established.
universalAnswers.readerRelevance: AI services depend on physical facilities using electricity and water; disclosure can make company environmental claims easier to inspect.
universalAnswers.affectedPeople: AI companies, communities near infrastructure, energy and water users, and countries whose access to AI benefits may differ.
universalAnswers.changesNow: The UN climate chief made concrete public requests; no legal obligation changed through the speech.
universalAnswers.uncertainty: Company responses, facility-level measurements, net climate effects and local cost effects remain unresolved.
universalAnswers.readerAction: For a company commitment, identify the facility, reporting period, measured resource use and decision tied to the claim.
universalAnswers.betterQuestion: What was measured at which facility and over what period, rather than is AI simply good or bad for the climate?

legal-policy.legalStatus: A policy speech and public request, not an enacted rule or order.
legal-policy.jurisdiction: The UNFCCC speech addresses AI industry leaders globally but creates no identified local legal obligation.
legal-policy.parties: Simon Stiell made the requests; AI company leaders are the intended audience; AP reports outside and industry perspectives.
legal-policy.allegationVsFinding: The requested actions are established by the transcript. Pollution, cost and potential-benefit claims remain attributed positions rather than findings of this article.
legal-policy.currentEffect: Public pressure and a clearer disclosure demand; no new legal duty or measured household effect.
legal-policy.unresolvedQuestions: Whether companies respond, what facility data show, and what climate or household effects can be measured.
legal-policy.nextMilestone: Any transcript correction, company response, reporting commitment or policy proposal resulting from the speech.

translation.newsVersionExact: UN climate chief Simon Stiell wants AI companies to make their energy and water use public, improve efficiency and power data centres with renewable energy.
translation.actualMeaningExact: These are demands on company leaders. The speech does not introduce a new rule or establish why a particular household’s electricity bill changed.
translation.mechanismExact: A dated account of a named facility’s electricity and water use gives the public something more specific to scrutinise.
translation.familiarExampleExact: A company promising to become greener has stated an intention. A dated account of a named facility’s electricity and water use gives the public something more specific to scrutinise.

learningConnections.learningPayoff: Explains the physical infrastructure behind AI electricity and water measurements.
